Fixes #68

## Summary

- Give recursive npm-alias removal an explicit `maxRetries: 5` and `retryDelay: 100` budget.
- Apply the shared cleanup behavior to both partial-install removal and corrupt-alias repair across ESM, CommonJS, universal, and generated root entry files.
- Add deterministic ESM and CommonJS regression coverage for the production `ENOTEMPTY` failure shape.
- Prepare patch release `8.14.4` and document the recovery behavior.

## Reproduction and automated verification

The regression fixture creates a corrupt npm alias, patches the fresh Node child process built-in `fs/promises.rm`, and injects `ENOTEMPTY` unless alias cleanup supplies the required recursive-rm retry budget.

Before the fix, both distributed builds fail with:

```text
Failed to remove corrupt npm alias '.../fixture-pkg-v-1.0.0'.
Caused by: ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '.../fixture-pkg-v-1.0.0'
```

After the fix, the fixture verifies the exact cleanup call:

```js
{
  recursive: true,
  force: true,
  maxRetries: 5,
  retryDelay: 100
}
```

It then confirms cleanup, reinstall, and import recovery complete successfully. Because `removePackageAlias()` is shared, the same retry budget also protects cleanup after failed npm installs.

## Tests

- `npm test -- --runInBand` — 45 suites, 349 tests passed
- `bun test` — 349 tests passed
- `deno test --allow-net --allow-env --allow-run --allow-read --allow-write --allow-sys` — 32 suites, 183 steps passed
- [Fresh CI run 30519863272](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/actions/runs/30519863272) — all six runtime/OS jobs passed for commit `dd7b034`
- `npm audit --omit=dev` — 0 vulnerabilities
- `npm pack --dry-run --json` — `use-m@8.14.4` package verified
- `git diff --check`
- root-entry and distributed-script synchronization checks passed

This is a non-UI filesystem-recovery fix, so screenshots are not applicable.
